contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you classified kinetic and potential energy. Today: how energy actually moves from one object to another!

Energy transfer happens when energy moves from one object or system to another, without changing form. When a moving pool ball hits a still one, kinetic energy transfers from the first ball to the second. When you touch a hot pan, thermal energy transfers from the pan to your hand. Describe a real example of energy transfer you've experienced, and identify what type of energy was involved.
You just described a real energy transfer! Tomorrow we'll learn about energy transformations, when energy changes form.

objectives: Define energy transfer as energy moving between objects without changing form
Describe a real personal example of energy transfer
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's kinetic/potential energy work.
2. Introduce energy transfer using the pool-ball and hot-pan examples.
3. Have the child describe their own real example.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's energy-transformation lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use a real physical demonstration (rolling one ball into another) to make transfer visible
Ready for more: ask the child to explain why the second pool ball starts moving using the idea of energy transfer, not just 'it got hit'
This lesson deliberately distinguishes 'transfer' (same form, different location) from tomorrow's 'transformation' (form changes) — name that distinction explicitly
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended reflection activity — check that the child describes a real, sensible energy-transfer example and correctly identifies the energy type involved (kinetic, thermal, etc.).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses NGSS Grade 6-8 Physical Science standard MS-PS3-2: energy transfer, continuing this week's energy thread.
